content.value: This note documents the creation of Gian-I Media, tracing its development from initial conceptualization through versions 0.5 to 1.0.

content.title: Let’s Start Here
summary: Explores the temple-themed branding of Gian-I Media.

content.title: Learning React.js
summary: Pursued React after internship feedback and missing the Parlour project.
Built the entire site from one HTML file using React and React Router.

content.title: General Structure
summary: Modeled the layout on Novak’s Hypermedia Navigator concept.
Framed the portfolio as a dream space with a persistent filtering navigator.

content.title: Filtration System
summary: Implemented multiple filter layers to scale cleanly to a large and growing project archive.
Filter settings persist across navigation until the page is reloaded.

content.title: Next Steps
summary: Finish the remaining 5 works to move from v0.5 to v0.6.
Redesign the filter UI for mobile resolutions.
Learn and integrate Next.js to improve searchability and performance.

content.title: Putting My Best Foot Forward
summary: Added 3 new projects to the portfolio, bringing the archive to 6 total works.
Increased the projected v1.0 archive to 10 total works.

content.title: Recursive Self-Improvement
summary: Completed and published all 10 projects planned for the portfolio’s version 1.0 archive.
Optimized the archive’s image assets by converting them to WebP, compressing them, and downscaling high-resolution files.

content.title: New Foundations
summary: Rebuilt Gian-I Media on Next.js with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS.
Adopted the full recommended stack after the Next.js tutorial bundled TypeScript and Tailwind into project setup.

content.title: Stylistic Adjustments
summary: Refined layout spacing and column proportions on work and note pages.
Improved accessibility and smoothed theme transitions with Tailwind.

content.title: Creative Technology
summary: Started sketching a personal stance on design and technology after GradEx.
Still forming; touches on craft, nature, and what technology is for.

content.title: Next Steps
summary: Nail down mobile filter UX.
Extend filtering to project tools and grid display options.
Refine dark mode, then push toward version 1.0.

content.title: Changes
summary: Extended filtering to project tools, refined the light and dark palettes, and clarified active filter controls in the header.

content.title: Reflections
summary: Shared screenshots from the original Figma file and looked back at early layout choices against the current build.
